listing.title: NORTIV 8 Men's Trail Running Shoes Wide Toe Box
listing.photos_note: Amazon listing scraped via Apify; 7 gallery images; no bullet points or size chart returned by the scraper. Breadcrumb: Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry > Men > Shoes > Athletic > Running > Trail Running

returns.comment: The shoes are comfy right out of the box and fit my foot well. I have owned them for about 2 months, with minimal runs during that time, and the tread near the balls of my feet are already gone. I wondered if they came that way and I just hadn't noticed, but I have a second pair I've bought as a backup and the tread is fully intact in the same region of that shoe. I know these are "trail" shoes, but after12 miles of pavement running in the last week I could easily see the difference in tread height between Sunday and Saturday. I know the shoes are "cheap", but I expected better durability in the tread as I feel the shoes are worn out with less than 50 miles of running.
returns.review_title: Comfy shoe, but the tread didn't last.

returns.comment: Sizing is correct. Toe box is definitely wider than average. Primary issue after 3 months of wear, including 1-3 mile walks on pavement and light trails a few times per week, is that the soles are already worn to the point where traction on wet pavement and loose gravel is significantly reduced, particularly at the ball and heel. Shoes from Hoka and Topo Athletic that I have purchased over the past couple of years also have this problem. The sole material is simply not durable. It is very disappointing to have to replace trail/walking shoes 2-3 times per year.

I have and use 4 different pairs of Trailrunners. These by far are hottest feeling shoes, they seem (look) to be a bit breathable but they just get so hot, even on cold days. I have no heat issues with Saucony Men's Excursion TR15,Tr16 or Tr17. The New Balance Men's 410 V9 also fine. The toe box is nice and wide but seems kinda flat, so the tops of your toes can rub a bit too much. Also I am not exactly sure why but the soles of the NORTIV 8 slip more than they should on smooth or wet surfaces, maybe its the lugs are the same height and mostly face the same direction. Two thumbs up for the wide toe box, but the rest of the shoe... just ok.
returns.review_title: For me the shoes were not breathable. A little flat at Toebox

returns.comment: These are comfortable and look nice but have a soft squishy feel that I find unstable. Not for me.
returns.review_title: Soft and squishy, not very stable

returns.comment: I am a big Altra Olympus user. But like most users I dont like to pay the higher price. I tried two pair of these Nortiv 8s in size 12. My opinion is that these Nortiv are not nearly as quality as the real Olympus. The standard insoles can be removed and your favorire insoles can be added. The shoes dont feel nearly as comfortable as the Olympus after a 4 mile jog. The tread is less and they dont feel as comfortable on the bottom of my feet. On the plus side the Nortiv is a pretty good clone. For easy use in walking and light running I think they can fill the bill. My opinion is at this low price give them a try and they might be good for you. YMMV
returns.review_title: Pretty close to the Olympus but not quite there.

returns.comment: The one thing that I absolutely know, is what shoe size I wear in several brands and I am very consistent. When I first began to wear Altra running shoes, both the company and the runner that told me about them said I should go up a half size from my normal tennis shoe size. I always wore a 10 wide so I went to a 10.5 altra and they fit perfect! Since 2017 I have worn nothing but 10.5 Altra Olympus tennis shoes. So I purchased the Nortiv 8 in a 10.5 as well since every review I read said this would be the right size for me. I took the left shoe out the box today and my foot was swimming in it. I put it sole to sole with my Olympus 5 and the shoe was huge. Easily an inch longer than my altra olympus 5. I probably should have checked the right shoe as well, but I wanted to return them brand new so I boxed it right back up. Now I haven't given up on this yet, as I liked the way the shoe looked so I am reordering them in a size 10 to see if it is a better fit. I did check the label on the left shoe, and it did say 10.5 so it was correct. When I put my foot in the shoe, it felt really big and my toe was way too far from the front of my shoe. Knowing I will immediately add powerstep insoles to the shoe, I thought maybe it just feels big because I haven't added the insole yet. However, when I put the shoe sole to sole with my Altra, and saw that it passed it up in the race by an inch, I said I don't think I can make these work. When the 10's come in, I will give them a try and see if the fit is better. Now the reason why I said the sizing seems to be all over the place is because I read several reviews that said people needed to size up from their normal size. WHAT? Size up? This shoe was gigantic for me in a 10.5. But I have no doubt, for those reviewers...that's what they needed to do. That's why I say sizing seems to be all over the place. The one other thing I noticed, is that the toe box on the Nortiv 8 looked even bigger than my Altra Olympus. If I can find the right length, that should not be a problem. My feet are fairly wide. I have fallen arches and must use an orthotic, so the extra room in the toe box will be welcome. But I cannot have that much extra length. I use a powerstep pinnacle insole with an added arch cookie and metatarsal bar so my feet do not constantly kill me. My podiatrist taught me to build up the insole this way and it has given me much relief. We will see if the size 10 works out better for me.
returns.review_title: Sizing seems to be all over the place!
